b2-argentinaba-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The River and the Port
b2-argentinaba-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Buenos Aires, and he asks why big ships anchored far from the shore.
b2-argentinaba-01.prompt: Tell Carlos why, with a formal phrase of cause.
cues: Use a formal phrase before the noun
b2-argentinaba-01.target: Debido a la poca profundidad del río, los barcos grandes anclaban lejos.
b2-argentinaba-01.english: Because of the shallow river, big ships anchored far away.
b2-argentinaba-01.canDo: I can describe how Buenos Aires grew along its river with formal phrases such as *mediante*, *debido a* and *a raíz de*.

b2-argentinaba-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Neighbourhood Filling Up
b2-argentinaba-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about the immigrants of Buenos Aires, and she asks what happened to the neighbourhoods.
b2-argentinaba-02.prompt: Tell Meg how the neighbourhood changed, step by step.
cues: Say what the neighbourhood was doing
b2-argentinaba-02.target: El barrio se iba llenando de familias que venían de Italia y de España.
b2-argentinaba-02.english: The neighbourhood was gradually filling up with families from Italy and Spain.
b2-argentinaba-02.canDo: I can describe how a neighbourhood changed little by little with *ir*, *seguir* and *venir* + gerund.

b2-argentinaba-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Tango and the UNESCO
b2-argentinaba-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to tango in a documentary, and he asks what UNESCO did with it.
b2-argentinaba-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what UNESCO did, naming who did it.
b2-argentinaba-03.target: El tango fue declarado Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial por la UNESCO en 2009.
b2-argentinaba-03.english: Tango was declared Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO in 2009.
b2-argentinaba-03.canDo: I can say who or what did something in the history of tango with the passive *ser* + participle.

b2-argentinaba-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Cafés of Buenos Aires
b2-argentinaba-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have read an article about the cafés and bookshops of Buenos Aires, and she asks for the main idea.
b2-argentinaba-04.prompt: Sum up the article for Meg and stress the main point.
cues: Say what the places are for
b2-argentinaba-04.target: En resumen, los cafés y las librerías son lugares para conversar.
b2-argentinaba-04.english: In short, the cafés and bookshops are places to talk.
b2-argentinaba-04.canDo: I can sum up an argument and stress the main point with *en resumen* and *lo más importante es que*.

b2-argentinaba-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Readers of Borges
b2-argentinaba-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a talk on Borges and Cortázar, and he asks if people still read them.
b2-argentinaba-05.prompt: Guess whether someone is reading Borges right now in the city.
b2-argentinaba-05.target: En una librería de la calle Corrientes habrá alguien comprando un libro de Borges.
b2-argentinaba-05.english: In a bookshop on Corrientes Street, someone is probably buying a book by Borges.
b2-argentinaba-05.canDo: I can guess about the present with the future of probability (*estará*, *habrá*, *serán*).

b2-argentinaba-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Buenos Aires in a Sentence
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a whole documentary about Buenos Aires, and she asks what you liked best.
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about the city, saying who did it.
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.target: La canción fue cantada por Carlos Gardel.
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.english: The song was sung by Carlos Gardel.
b2-argentinaba-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the history and culture of Buenos Aires, from the port to the tango.
